messages:
Riley: Quick preflight for the webinar visuals: can we land a single slide that tells the speed vs unit-cost story in <10s? Thinking a scatter + trend line, with a separate tiny p99 inset. Need copy, data callouts, and routing for CTAs.
Tariq: Yes. Scatter: x = median latency (ms), y = $ per 1k tokens. Trend line shows cost/latency tradeoff. Inset: p99 distribution as small boxplot. Keep labels tight.
Jules: Also include two badges: "Hosted API" and "Dedicated (reserved)" with color-coded markers so we can call out routing benefits. People ask which to pick.
Nina: Headline option: "How we reconcile speed and spend for production LLMs". Subhead: "Benchmark across real prompts, median and tail latency, and unit economics."
BenchBot: Bench run summary uploaded to artifact store: median latencies [hosted: 92ms, dedicated: 68ms], p99 [hosted: 420ms, dedicated: 150ms], unit cost $/1k [hosted: 3.4, dedicated: 2.05]. Full CSV: https://bench.redwood/runs/5532109876.csv
Tariq: Add a tiny caption explaining batching and cache posture: "results use dynamic batching, prefix cache enabled where applicable". Also note model family and quantization.
Riley: Good call. Jules, can you do the Figma mock by EOD Fri? Also need the callouts for p99 impact on UX (e.g., token-heavy customers).
Jules: On it. I'll put two variants: one with a larger inset and one with an annotated line calling out the p99 delta.
Nina: Marketing copy tweak: avoid absolute claims like "faster and cheaper". Use "lower median latency and reduced unit cost under common configs". Also include a one-line methodology link.
GrowthOps: Routing plan: webinar signups -> marketing nurture sequence; "request dedicated" clicks -> sales SDR queue with tag "heatmap-demo"; "view methodology" -> docs.utm=heatmap_preflight. We'll attach source tag for attribution.
BenchBot: Methodology snippet to include in notes:
```json
{"model_family":"rw-open-3b","seq_len":512,"batching":"dynamic","cache":"prefix_kv","quant":"int8"}
```
Tariq: Perfect. Also prepare a 2-line FAQ for the slide notes: 1) What workloads were tested? 2) How do I get similar performance?
Riley: Action items: Jules - Figma variants; Tariq - p99 callouts & FAQ lines; GrowthOps - inbound routing YAML + tags; BenchBot - confirm CSV link and reproducibility steps. I'll assemble the slide and circulate Mon morning.
Jules: ack. I'll mock both headline treatments and the color palette for hosted vs dedicated. :paintbrush:
BenchBot: CSV checksum: sha256:abc123...; reproducibility doc: https://confluence.redwood/bench/5532109876-repro.
Nina: I'm going to A/B test two email lead lines: A) "See our heatmap: speed vs spend in real workloads" B) "How to keep latency tight without blowing your token budget" 4 that should help open rate.
GrowthOps: Adding utm_campaign=heatmap_preflight and utm_medium=email to outbound links. Will post routing YAML for review.
Riley: Great, thanks team. Final ask: keep the slide readable for execs  one quick takeaway + where to click for deep-dive.
